name: Verbalized Sampling
description: Training-free prompting technique to unlock LLM creative diversity by asking the model to verbalize a probability distribution over k candidate responses instead of generating a single answer. Mitigates the mode collapse that RLHF/DPO bakes into aligned LLMs via typicality bias. Recovers up to 66.8% of base-model pretraining diversity at inference time, with 1.6-2.1x diversity gains on creative writing tasks. Apply this skill at every creative/synthesis touchpoint where output reads as predictable or conventional. Bigger models (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus, GPT-5.5) benefit more. COMPOSES WITH: recommendation-architect (content diversity), html-deliverable-composer (presentation diversity across the five HTML-generation layers — visual layout, IA, diagram type, interaction pattern, iconography). The five-layer composition is documented in plans/html-as-default-output-uplift.md.

name: HTML Deliverable Composer
description: Generates NXT/NU brand-locked, self-contained HTML artifacts (briefs, explainers, reports, playgrounds, approach-pickers) as the canonical output format for human-review deliverables. Replaces Markdown for any output a human reads and shares. Encodes the NXT design system as CSS variables, the 8 information types (tables, design, illustrations, code, interactions, workflows, spatial, images), 5-7 SVG diagram recipes, the print stylesheet, and the 'Copy as prompt' round-trip helper. COMPOSES WITH verbalized-sampling (mandatory) at five generation layers: visual layout, information architecture, diagram type per SVG, interaction pattern, iconography vocabulary. Loads `verbalized-sampling/SKILL.md` first then prepends its own content. Triggered by #brief, #explainer, #report, #playground, #approaches, and #artifacts (library). Supports a --variants k modifier (k=1-6) that emits the article's 'show me k' grid-picker pattern inline. PENDING: skill file to be created in Sprint H1 of the HTML-as-default uplift rollout. Plan at humans-in-control-research/plans/html-as-default-output-uplift.md.

name: Reinforcement Inference
description: Anchored re-ask pattern: when a generation's selfAssessment.overallConfidence is LOW/MEDIUM or validation fails, the regen pins the prior answer into the prompt and only revises the flagged claims, instead of starting from scratch. Closes the R3 gap from plans/reinforcement-inference-uplift.md. The wrapper lives in services/reinforcementInference.ts and is invoked at 10 regen sites in geminiService.ts plus the uncertainty ledger at wiki/synthesis/uncertainty-ledger.md.

name: Recommendation Architect
description: Generate consulting-grade AI tool recommendations grounded in client-uploaded docs and stakeholder constraints. Extracts named stakeholders, their priorities and non-starters, technology-stack preferences, dependency flags (named initiatives), and existing-system reuse from the user's prompt and uploads — then produces 5-12 distinct recommendations honoring all constraints, with implementation depth a senior consultant would defend in a client meeting. Triggered explicitly by #recommendations. COMPOSES WITH verbalized-sampling (VS-Multi pattern) — emits two concept groups: concepts_defensible_consensus (full distribution, k=5) + concepts_non_obvious_bets (deep-tail p<0.05, k=5). The chat handler loads BOTH skills at runtime: vs-skill + recommendation-architect + topic instructions.

name: Wiki Query Expander
description: Multiplies semantic-retrieval recall by expanding a single user question into 3-4 conceptually distinct query variants, firing one fetch_wiki_articles call per variant, and merging results by url_hash. Exploits the underlying OpenAI/Gemini embedding layer — each variant hits a different vector-space neighborhood. Use for retrieval-intent messages: 'find', 'search the archive', 'what does the wiki say', 'pull everything on', 'dig through the wiki'.

name: Wiki Reranker
description: Cross-encoder reranker: after fetch_wiki_articles returns candidates, Claude re-reads the user's question and scores each article 1-5 on direct intent relevance, citing only articles scoring 4+. Replaces the need for a Cohere rerank API subscription. Essential when retrieval returns near-duplicates, off-topic siblings, or surface-semantic-match-but-wrong-intent results. Emits a transparent rerank table so the user sees Claude's scoring before it's used.

name: Wiki Synthesizer
description: For broad questions spanning multiple articles: retrieves from 3 distinct angles (root cause, impact, response), extracts verbatim quotes per angle, clusters quotes by cross-angle theme, and emits a Minto-style synthesis (answer first, 3 supporting themes with convergent patterns, evidence gaps named). Pairs with semantic embeddings because each angle hits a different neighborhood — the cross-angle pattern IS the synthesis. Use for 'synthesize', 'tell me everything about', 'build a picture', 'what's the story'. Do not use for narrow fact-check.

name: NXT Visual Renderer
description: NXT Humans Design System v3.0 — canonical layout, density, and quote-handling contract for the 18 web slide templates + PPTX export. Render-contract: always loaded alongside any content skill when slide intent is detected. Covers NXT and NU brand variants — colors resolve per brand, layout geometry is shared. Option B density upgrade: per-template IMPLICATION, full-sentence smart-clipped quotes with role attribution, plus template-specific extensions (PATTERN SIGNAL, per-theme SIGNAL, MEANS/MATTERS, CONVERGENT INSIGHT, LESSON, COMPARABLES, IMPACT GRID, EVIDENCE strip, CONTEXT PARAGRAPH, CORROBORATING DATA).

name: Persona Architect
description: JTBD + Cooper Goal Hierarchy. Reject generic demographics. Synthesize behavioral archetypes exclusively from raw corpus data. Must include verbatim user quotes directly mapped to Pain Points and Motivations.

name: Strategy Author
description: Rumelt's Kernel (Diagnosis, Guiding Policy, Coherent Actions). 18-section Minto Pyramid narrative. Every strategic pillar linked to measurable economic outcome. Ruthless SCR formatting.

name: Competitive Analyst
description: Porter's Forces / Blue Ocean positioning — domain-agnostic, works for any industry where the corpus names peers (SaaS vendors, health systems, retailers, banks, universities, CPG brands, etc.). REQUIRED: extract at least 4 NAMED competitors from the corpus (never 'Industry Average' or 'Peers Collective' — those indicate the corpus didn't actually name any). Each row carries per-capability scoring 1-5 AND a specific evidence note grounded in that industry's language (revenue, ARR, endowment, bed count, GMV, AUM, etc.). Columns MUST include one-line capability definitions. Scale MUST include named maturity levels appropriate to the domain (e.g., Absent/Ad-hoc/Defined/Managed/Optimized for consulting; Basic/Defined/Managed/World-class for SaaS; Manual/Semi-automated/Automated/Real-time for ops). Highlight the subject row. Refuse sparse 3-row matrices.

name: Service Blueprint Mapper
description: Bitner service blueprint adapted for 16:9 slides — works for any multi-stage journey (enterprise onboarding, patient care, retail purchase, loan origination, donor lifecycle, trial-to-paid, claim filing). REQUIRED structure: 4 stages MAX (5+ overflows), every stage carries duration + emotion + all four lanes (customer / frontstage / backstage / support). Duration units match the domain (days, weeks, sprints, care episodes, quarters). FailPoint flags only on stages where the process genuinely breaks. keyInsight MUST quantify the business cost of the fail points in the domain's native metric (ACV, ARR, readmissions, GMV, retention dollars, claim cycle time). Tie friction to specific numbers from the corpus — never 'customers are frustrated' without the cost attached.

name: Technology Architecture Generator
description: C4 Model (Context & Containers). Generate 10-section node and integration mapping. Explicitly define system constraints, integration payloads, and boundary limits from technical corpus documents.

name: PRD Compiler
description: SVPG / Cagan Framework: define the Why before the What. Feature-level requirements heavily grounded in cited user quotes and identified market gaps. Epics decomposed using MECE logic.

name: Roadmap Builder
description: Now/Next/Later Strategic Sequencing. Avoid rigid Gantt charts; use outcome-based horizons. Prioritization mathematically justified by economic value, feasibility, and risk with specific corpus citations.

name: Gap Analysis Evaluator
description: Gartner 1-5 Maturity Assessment across technical and operational vectors. Current-state baselines and target-state goals substantiated by quantitative evidence and cited institutional deficiencies.

name: Tech Audit Inspector
description: COBIT / TEI Audit. Comprehensive systems inventory. Explicitly flag siloed data risks, security vulnerabilities, and redundancy costs backed by evidence.

name: Theme Analyst
description: 6-Lens Thematic Analysis. Extract strategic themes from multi-source research corpus. Each theme grounded in convergent evidence from multiple named sources with verbatim quotes.

name: Strategic Report Writer
description: McKinsey-format strategic whitepaper. Rumelt's Kernel + 20 named sources + case studies + social evidence. Full unrestricted narrative layer with no character budgets.

name: Evidence Curator
description: Surfaces a single powerful verbatim quote with full attribution and source context. Used when ONE piece of testimony carries the argument. Owns the block-quote slide template.

name: Case Study Analyst
description: Structures real-world examples with FIVE data vectors (never just one stat) — domain-agnostic, pulls from whatever named entity appears in the corpus (company, vendor, health system, university, agency, bank, retailer, NGO). Required: subject + subjectMeta using that domain's sizing vocabulary (ARR, endowment, headcount, beds, stores, AUM, branches), explicit timeframe in the domain's unit (quarters, academic years, sprints, care episodes), investment (cost + team size / capex / program budget), the full Challenge/Approach/Outcome narrative with at least one quantified detail per block, a hero keyMetric PLUS 3-4 supportingMetrics, and ideally a verbatim pullQuote from someone inside the case. If the corpus only supports a single stat, refuse the case study and use stat-row instead. Pulls from named organizations ONLY — never 'a leading bank' or 'a health system' (those indicate the corpus lacks a real case).

name: Benchmark Reporter
description: Extracts 3-4 hero metrics with named sources and renders them as oversized statistics. Every number carries an attribution — no hero stats without citations. Owns the stat-row slide template.

name: Deck Composer
description: The single versioned authority for #slides / #strategy / #presentation deck composition (DECK MODE, SLIDES archetype registry): archetype selection by content shape, gate-enforced visual floor and variety rules, narrative arc (Minto / Rumelt / SCQA), title craft, subject discipline, the infographic-exhibit depth contract, reference-deck voice; section 8 carries the legacy GOLD Slide-object contract (12 content block types) folded from deck-narrative-composer on 2026-10-01.

name: NXT Visual Renderer
description: NXT Design System rendering engine. Stark White Template, anti-slop business flat minimalism. 7 layout patterns, color system, typography, anti-slop checklist. Generates slides and visual components with mandatory delimiters.

name: NXT Humans Slide Templates
description: The 10 canonical slide templates, available in two visual brands chosen by hashtag in the user's prompt: #NXT (NXT Humans — teal + chartreuse, default) or #NU (Northeastern University — near-black + Huskies Red). Every slide emitted by the chat picks one of the 10 templates, fills the data shape, and the web preview + PPTX export + PDF export all render from the SAME data for pixel parity. Templates: persona-card (persona-architect), recommendation (strategy-author), theme-cluster (theme-analyst), competitive-matrix (competitive-analyst), block-quote (evidence-curator), case-study (case-study-analyst), principles (strategy-author), stat-row (benchmark-reporter), timeline (roadmap-builder), section-divider (deck-composer). Emit :::slide template=NAME [brand=nxt|nu] blocks — never freelance a layout.

name: Source Ranker
description: Ranks any candidate source set by four orthogonal dimensions wiki-reranker doesn't cover — credibility (peer-review / publication editorial standards), recency (current/dated/outdated tuned to topic volatility), argument-relevance (direct/tangential/weak — distinct from intent-relevance), and the binding citation-protocol classification external/client/synthetic. Emits per-source Use/Verify/Cut verdicts, the top 3 to build the argument on, the one to cut, the missing source type that would make the argument stronger, and a final external-ratio diagnostic that gates the deliverable against the 60%-external floor. Auto-loads via composes_with on every research-deliverable skill — the user never has to ask for citation-quality enforcement.

name: Contradiction Finder
description: Surfaces where sources in the retrieval set actively disagree on a specific claim, theme, or finding — instead of flattening contradictions into smoothed consensus. Returns the surface consensus, 3 specific contradictions with both sides quoted verbatim (paraphrase is forbidden), the single weakest claim in the material, the field's real unresolved debate, and a calibrated confidence verdict (High/Medium/Low) that drives whether the deliverable should cite forward, narrow the claim, or re-retrieve. Directly raises the Evidence Hierarchy dimension of the hic-output-qa rubric. Auto-loaded via composes_with on heavy-synthesis deliverables (theme-analyst, strategy-author, competitive-analyst, gap-analysis-evaluator, strategic-report-writer).

name: Second Order Thinker
description: Maps the second-order, third-order, unintended, and feedback-loop consequences of any strategic recommendation or decision. First-order effects are the obvious 'if we do X then Y'. Second-order is what happens after that. Third-order is where unintended consequences emerge. Feedback loops are where the system either amplifies the original move or quietly undoes it. Forces three moves ahead per recommendation. Names one unintended consequence. Surfaces the amplifying-or-undermining loop. Distinguishes a competent recommendation from a partner-grade one. Auto-loaded via composes_with on strategy-author, recommendation-architect, roadmap-builder, and strategic-report-writer — anywhere the deliverable produces ACTIONS (not diagnoses).

name: Slide Title Lab
description: Generates 15 candidate action-titles for every body slide across 8 distinct title formats (data-led, contrast, mechanism, stakes, named-entity, finding, decision, before-after), scores each against the validate_titles.py rules (>=8 words, has data point AND action verb, no topic labels, no banned slop, complete sentence, under 120 chars), and returns the top 3 plus the weakest pattern across all 15. Replaces one-shot slide-title generation with a generate-many + rank pattern that lifts action-title compliance directly. Auto-loaded via composes_with on deck-composer and strategic-report-writer — every slide title goes through this gate before the deck renders. Section dividers, cover slides, and persona cards are exempt (they follow their own naming convention).

name: Human Voice Editor
description: Positive-voice counterpart to the anti-slop banlists: how good consulting prose reads (active voice, omit needless words, short concrete words, specificity, burstiness, take a position, earn emphasis, trust the reader, reuse precise terms, Orwell rule-6 override). Humanizes themes, headlines, deliverables, and chat replies. SkillOpt-trained.
